audit.whatIsWrong: The "Lvl 2-3" spike promises a Devour: "At 3 An Acquired Taste stacks your Tongue Lash stun lands and you can Devour Jayce mid-air". whys[2], the level-3 stage, does the same: "Tongue Lash stun into Devour removes Jayce from the fight".
audit.why: Devour is Tahm Kench's ultimate. It does not exist before level 6. At levels 2-3 the three-stack payoff is the Tongue Lash STUN and nothing else, which is a completely different-sized threat — a stun he can be walked away from versus a multi-second removal. Selling the level-2 window as a Devour window invites a Tahm Kench to commit into a ranged poke champion on the promise of a button he does not have. Against Jayce specifically that commit costs Flash, which the entry elsewhere correctly tells him to hoard. Separately, 'Devour Jayce mid-air' asserts an interaction with To the Skies! that Riot's text does not describe and I could not verify; I removed the claim rather than restate it.
audit.corrected: Before 6 the payoff is the stun alone. Devour enters the plan at 6.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — R Devour is the ultimate slot; P 'At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion' (a stack gate, not a level gate, but the ability itself is still R)

audit.whatIsWrong: Three passages route the level-6 plan through "Abyssal Voyage": spikes[3] "before your Abyssal Voyage can threaten him", mid "At level 6 Abyssal Voyage arrives but it does not solve the range problem directly — what it does is make Jayce paranoid about tower dives and roams", whys[4] "before your Abyssal Voyage is even up".
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is the pre-2021-rework ultimate and is not on the live champion. Tahm Kench's level 6 is Devour. The mid passage is the worst of the three because it builds a whole psychological read on top of the phantom ability — 'makes Jayce paranoid about tower dives and roams' is an effect of a global that does not exist, and a Jayce player has no reason to feel any of it.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is Devour, gated at three An Acquired Taste stacks — a lockdown, not a roam threat.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — R Devour, W Abyssal Dive, no global ability in kit

audit.whatIsWrong: mid warns the player not to spend Tongue Lash "into his Hyper Charge cancel or his hammer-stance dodge".
audit.why: Neither thing exists. Hyper Charge is the CANNON-stance W — a burst of attack speed for several attacks. It cancels nothing and it is not a defensive tool. And Jayce has no dodge in hammer stance or any other stance. What he actually has in hammer stance is Thundering Blow, which knocks the target back a short distance, and the Mercury Hammer transform itself, whose first attack in that form deals bonus magic damage while the form grants him bonus Armor and Magic Resist. Those are the real reasons a Tongue Lash can be wasted at close range, and they call for different timing than dodging a phantom cancel.
audit.corrected: Thundering Blow's knockback and the Mercury Hammer transform's resistances, not a Hyper Charge cancel or a dodge.
sources: champ-data/_kits/jayce.json — W Cannon Stance 'Hyper Charge: Gains a burst of energy, increasing Attack Speed to maximum for several attacks'; E Hammer Stance 'Thundering Blow: Deals magic damage to an enemy and knocks them back a short distance'; R 'Mercury Hammer... increasing Armor and Magic Resist'

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[2] tells the player to fight "where his Acceleration Gate has no wall to anchor".
audit.why: Acceleration Gate is not anchored to terrain and has no wall interaction at all — it is a free-placed gate that speeds up allies who pass through it and, critically, empowers a Shock Blast fired through it with increased missile speed, RANGE and damage. The invented wall rule would send a Tahm Kench to fight in open ground believing he has neutralised the gate, when open ground is exactly where a gated Shock Blast has the most room to reach him.
audit.corrected: The gate has no terrain requirement. What matters is whether Shock Blast is fired through it — that is the range and damage amplifier.
sources: champ-data/_kits/jayce.json — E Cannon Stance: 'Deploys an Acceleration Gate increasing the Move Speed of all allied champions who pass through it. If Shock Blast is fired through the gate the missile speed, range, and damage will increase.'

audit.whatIsWrong: Hextech Capacitor is never mentioned, and the entry repeatedly describes Jayce disengaging "the instant you walk up" without saying how.
audit.why: Every weapon swap grants Jayce Move Speed. That is the mechanism behind the disengage the entry keeps describing, and it means the escape is on the transform cooldown (6s) rather than on any of his spell cooldowns. For a champion with no dash, knowing the disengage is tied to the stance swap — and therefore that it is available roughly every six seconds — is the difference between timing a walk-up and giving up on one.
audit.corrected: Name Hextech Capacitor: swapping weapons gives him Move Speed, and the swap is a 6s cooldown.
sources: champ-data/_kits/jayce.json — P Hextech Capacitor: 'When Jayce swaps weapons he gains Move Speed for a short duration'; R cooldown 6

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers say to track Shock Blast without ever giving its cooldown, and the entry never notes that Jayce's Q and E have SIX ranks rather than five.
audit.why: Shock Blast is 16/14/12/10/8/6 and Acceleration Gate / Thundering Blow is 20/18/16/14/12/10. At the levels the mid section covers, Shock Blast is around 12-14s — a real punish window, not the unanswerable spam the text implies. The six-rank scaling is also why the lane gets steadily harder to walk into rather than easier: most laners' poke cooldowns bottom out at rank 5.
audit.corrected: State the Shock Blast cooldown where the text tells the player to wait it out.

audit.why: 55.65% over 868 games. edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are Jayce's window to extend any lead he built — he can poke freely through gates and disengage with his knockback the instant you walk up. Sit on the wave, let your grey health regenerate between trades, and do not burn your Tongue Lash into his Hyper Charge cancel or his hammer-stance dodge. At level 6 Abyssal Voyage arrives but it does not solve the range problem directly — what it does is make Jayce paranoid about tower dives and roams, which lets you reset the threat dynamic back to the lane. Fish for a pre-6 stack window near a slow push: if he swaps to Mercury Hammer to shove, his cannon-stance poke range disappears and your 3-stack stun window opens.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are Jayce's window to extend any lead he built — he can poke freely through gates and disengage with Thundering Blow's knockback the instant you walk up. Sit on the wave, let your grey health regenerate between trades, and remember every stance swap hands him Hextech Capacitor move speed on a 6s timer. At level 6 Devour arrives but it does not solve the range problem directly — it only exists once three An Acquired Taste stacks are on him, so the stun still has to land first. Fish for a stack window near a slow push: if he swaps to Mercury Hammer to shove, his cannon-stance poke range disappears and your 3-stack window opens.

I found it in jayce, gwen, illaoi, irelia, karma, kassadin and kayle inside my own slice alone; the full list from a scripted scan is akshan, ambessa, cassiopeia, chogath, darius, galio, gangplank, garen (x2), gragas, gwen, illaoi, irelia, jayce, karma, kassadin, kayle, kennen, ksante, malphite, mordekaiser, nasus, rumble, sejuani, sett, shen, sion (x2), sylas, teemo, trundle, tryndamere, urgot, vayne, vladimir, volibear, warwick, yasuo, yone, yorick. This is worth a single scripted fix rather than 40 hand edits — every one of them oversells the pre-6 window to the player and several of them, like this matchup, use it to justify committing Flash. Second: this entry had an EMPTY defects array and an empty suspectNames array in the packet, yet contains five separate factual errors. The detector's clean bill of health should not be read as a reason to skip a matchup.
